newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia opposition prepares to take on Milosevic.
newsitem.headline: Serbia opposition prepares to take on Milosevic.

text.p: Serbia's opposition kept up their protests on Friday as parliament prepared to sit in extraordinary session to pass a bill meeting their main demand, the reinstatement of opposition gains in last year's local elections.

The protests that began three months ago continued as opposition leaders, on the verge of gaining this major concession, raised their sights to taking on autocratic President Slobodan Milosevic in parliamentary and presidential elections later this year.
In bright sunlight, about 15,000 students marched through Belgrade, keeping up their protests until parliament meets on Tuesday and passes a bill reinstating opposition election gains.
The official Yugoslav news agency Tanjug said the bill, approved by Milosevic's Socialist government on Wednesday, reached parliament on Friday ahead of Tuesday's meeting.

Milosevic had suddenly announced three days ago he was asking parliament to approve a new law recognising the opposition's local election victories, a central plank of their campaign for democratic reform.
"We will wait for the decision of parliament but until then the demonstrations will continue for sure," opposition Democratic Party spokesman Slobodan Vuksanovic told a news conference on Friday.
Even at this late stage, the issue of recognising opposition gains in local elections last November 17 --- annulled by the Socialists on the grounds of "irregularities" --- seemed far from clear cut.

There appeared to be confusion over what opposition gains would be recognised, and whether these included not only nine Belgrade municipalities listed in the report of an OSCE fact-finding mission last December, but New Belgrade council as well.

The draft law, as read out on state radio and television, mentions Belgrade without going into detail, but opposition leaders have said Milosevic has omitted New Belgrade municipality and they would put forward an amendment to the bill.

Vuksanovic, echoing remarks of Zajedno leaders, said the opposition would not attend Tuesday's extraordinary session, where the Socialists are two short of a clear majority but can count on ethnic minority representatives.
Even if the draft is deemed to omit New Belgrade, how the opposition would submit an amendment without putting in an appearance during the session has not been explained.
Neither the socialists nor the opposition won an absolute majority in New Belgrade, but the opposition accuses the Socialists of having taken over the local council anyway.
"If new attempts to forge the results and cheat the people arose," Vuksanovic said, "demonstrations will have a new dimension and will become more intensive."
Opposition politician Vuk Draskovic told demonstrators on Thursday night that New Belgrade was missing from a list of disputed results parliament was expected to endorse on Tuesday.

"It is already certain that they (the Socialists) have decided to swallow New Belgrade (municipality)," Draskovic said. "We shall demand that the government bill be amended to include a recognition of our results in New Belgrade."
Opposition leaders meanwhile clearly had Milosevic in their sights as they prepared the ground for parliamentary and presidential elections due by the end of this year.
"We must never forget that we have not achieved a full-scale democratisation of Serbia," opposition politician Zoran Djindjic told Thursday's 50,000-strong rally.
"The main preconditions for removing Milosevic in a democratic manner are fair election conditions, for which we need free media and a full rule of law," Djindjic declared.
Opposition leader Vesna Pesic echoed the concern for the long-term political future of Serbia.
"Democracy has become a way of life. We can no longer live without fighting for democracy," she told supporters.
Last Sunday Milosevic sent his paramilitary police in to clear the streets of demonstrators. Repeated baton charges left scores injured and prompted an international outcry.
